body:
@hippogyz my guess is that you are leaking a node that is getting cleaned up by the garbage collector. As a result, the free function will get called from whatever thread the garbage collector is run on, which likely isn't the rendering thread. 

You need to manually free the rendering resources in order to avoid this

> [@hippogyz](https://github.com/hippogyz) my guess is that you are leaking a node that is getting cleaned up by the garbage collector. As a result, the free function will get called from whatever thread the garbage collector is run on, which likely isn't the rendering thread.
> 
> You need to manually free the rendering resources in order to avoid this

Well...I tried to comment some codes in the MRP, and I found this line caused resources leaking:
``` C#

    public override void _RenderCallback(int effectCallbackType, RenderData renderData)
    {
        var renderSceneBuffers = renderData.GetRenderSceneBuffers() as RenderSceneBuffersRD;
        ... // comment rest of codes in _RenderCallback still triggers the Error
```

It seems `RenderData.GetRenderSceneBuffers()` leaks any resources internally? 


EDIT: I tried other members in `RenderData`, only the `RenderSceneBuffers` will triggers the error. Maybe the problem is that the `RenderSceneBuffers` is a `RefCounted`?

A workaround: 
  1. rewrite your `CompositorEffect` with gdscript.
  2. [manually instantiate it in C#.](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/scripting/cross_language_scripting.html)
  3. when you no longer need it, dereference the `GodotObject` instance. 
  4. now Editor won't throw errors when scene switching. 

Example:  [test_free_rid.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19740308/test_free_rid.zip)
Enable/disable the `UseCSharp` flag in `LoadEffect.cs` to see the difference between C# case and gdscript case.

Is there a proper solution to this other than a workaround? I have run into the same thing and while it "seemingly" doesn't cause any issues it is incredibly annoying to be spammed with errors everytime I open the editor.

Looking at the provided stack trace, it looks like the finalizer is being executed. As @clayjohn said, finalizers are executed on a different thread from the rendering thread, so if these resources must be freed on the rendering thread you'll need to properly dispose them to avoid this.

The finalizer is meant to be a fallback, you shouldn't rely on it to clean up resources for you. Instead, disposable objects should always be properly disposed of, by calling the [`Dispose`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.idisposable.dispose) method or with the [`using`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/statements/using) statement [^1].

@hippogyz, as you suspected, it looks like you are not disposing the `RenderSceneBuffersRD` instance. Consider adding a `using` statement, like this:

```csharp
using var renderSceneBuffers = renderData.GetRenderSceneBuffers() as RenderSceneBuffersRD;
```

This should ensure the resource is properly disposed when you are done using it, instead of leaving it to the garbage collector.

[^1]: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/garbage-collection/using-objects

It works for me. Thanks!

But there is one thing I don't understand: 
In this case, the inherit order is `RefCounted` -> `RenderSceneBuffers` -> `RenderSceneBuffersRD`. But in my understanding, C# `as` won't create a new instance for this object. So `using` statement will actually dispose the `RenderSceneBuffers` which is a member of input parameter `RenderData` in the `_RenderCallback()` function. Does it make the object's lifetime unmatched with its scope? 

(EDIT: I read the `GodotObject.cs` and `runtime_interop.cpp`. It seems dispose C# object only reduce the ref-count but won't free the object instantaneous? )

Anyway, maybe using `using` statement for C# CompositorEffect should be noted in document.

When you get a reference to a `RefCounted` object in C#, it increments the reference count; disposing it decrements the reference count. When the reference count reaches 0, the resource is freed.

You are correct that the `as` operator doesn't create new instances and therefore it doesn't affect the reference count. It's just a cast that returns `null` if the cast fails, instead of throwing an exception like a regular cast would.

You are also correct that you usually shouldn't dispose input parameters, since you don't normally own them. This depends on the specific scenario, but it makes sense to assume that if you didn't create the instance you receive as an input parameter, you probably aren't responsible for disposing it.

However, in this particular case, the instance we're referring to is not the `renderData` input parameter itself. The method `GetRenderSceneBuffers()` returns a new `RefCounted` instance. This means `GetRenderSceneBuffers()` is incrementing the reference count, and you are now responsible for disposing it. The fact that this method is called on an input parameter is not relevant to the ownership of the returned object.

> Anyway, maybe using `using` statement for C# CompositorEffect should be noted in document.

The `using` statement is relevant for all C# types that implement the `IDisposable` interface, not just `CompositorEffect`, and it's more of a .NET concept than a Godot one. That said, I think it makes sense to add a note about it (and link to [Microsoft's documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/garbage-collection/using-objects)) for the types where it's specially relevant such as those that need to be disposed in the rendering thread.

Thanks for explaining. This issue should be closed now.

I've added [a comment to the Compositor document](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-docs-user-notes/discussions/261#discussioncomment-13572230).

 And for someone who meets the same question: **use `using` statement for `RenderSceneBuffersRD`**, i.e.
> `using var renderSceneBuffers = renderData.GetRenderSceneBuffers() as RenderSceneBuffersRD;`
